name: meta-theory-author
description: Specialization of meta-expert-author for skills built exclusively on peer-reviewed academic sources. Produces theory-focused skills with DOI discipline, retraction checks, and Keshav three-pass reading. Inherits wave arc and dispatch; overrides sourcing, verification, axis model, and file shape. Ships executable verification harness (verify_skill.py) that validates frontmatter, resolves DOIs, checks retraction status, and tests URL liveness. Peers with meta-expert-author.
invariants: All invariants of meta-expert-author apply unless explicitly overridden.
Sources are peer-reviewed academic or preprint-academic only — no blog posts, product docs, YouTube non-academic content, or industry white papers.
Each reference file in works/ summarizes exactly one paper. Figures/ files are mixed-mode capability-synthesis across multiple papers.
DOI is required for works/ files. If no DOI exists, the file uses the stablest identifier and flags the DOI absence.
Retraction status is verified at Wave 1 authoring and at every refresh.
Preprint version is tracked; refresh checks whether a preprint was published (version supersession).
Quoted material stays within fair-use budgets (≤100 words continuous, or ≤10% of a short paper).
SKILL.md uses the canon-curation 'greatest hits' shape with required 'unresolved debates' and 'replication status' sections.
Agents MUST use WebSearch and WebFetch to find and read every paper. Summary from prior-knowledge alone is forbidden.
Keshav's three-pass reading method is the minimum standard: pass 1 + pass 2 for every file; pass 3 for coverage: deep.
Paper-type is declared in frontmatter (empirical / theoretical / methodological / review / meta-analysis / position).
Author-canon (multi-paper trajectories) handled via mixed-mode: figures/ axis synthesis + works/ one-paper-per-file.
Field-specific adaptations are applied per skill's primary field.
Disagreements are surfaced explicitly: contested claims do not appear as consensus in SKILL.md.
Produced skills MUST pass tools/verify_skill.py before v1.0.0 signoff. Post-wave verification recommended; 6-month refresh mandatory with --network.
notes: Inherits from meta-expert-author v1.3.0. v1.0-v1.3 completed the pure doctrine layer. v1.4 ships tools/verify_skill.py — an executable Python verifier (580 lines, stdlib + PyYAML) that validates the invariants against a produced skill. Runs locally (frontmatter checks, date format, staleness, peer paths, quote budgets) or with --network (Crossref DOI resolution, retraction via update-to field, arxiv ID validity, URL liveness). Smoke-tested against ref-dashboard and surfaced 162 broken peer-path references that human review missed. The meta-skill is now doctrinally complete AND mechanically verifiable.
